 Alabama Basketball vs Kennesaw State: 3 Keys, How to Watch
 Alabama has one final tune-up before things get tough.
 by Joshua Chatham Nov 17, 2026, 4:54 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Old friend Antoine Pettway brings his undefeated Kennesaw State Owls into Coleman tonight, looking to continue steady improvement in his fourth season. Last season the Owls finished 21-14, captured the Conference USA Tournament championship, and earned a 14-seed in the NCAA Tournament. They gave Gonzaga all they wanted before falling by nine points in the opening round.
 Pettway’s squad is comfortable running at a Nate Oats pace, and in fact have averaged slightly more possessions in their games thus far than Alabama. And, like the Tide, Kennesaw State loves to shoot the three. Unfortunately they’ve only made 29% on 34 attempts per game thus far. What the Owls have done effectively is rebound the basketball, something that Alabama has struggled with at times this season.
 The transfer portal took a significant bite out of the roster, with three starters departing for greener pastures. Leading scorer and First-Team All-Conference USA guard RJ Johnson left for Mississippi State, while 6’8” forward Braedan Lue headed to Tennessee, and leading rebounder Frankquon Sherman is now at High Point.
 Thus far, the replacements have looked solid enough to win all four games, but the level of competition hasn’t been terribly strong. The Owls have started the season with a nail-biter vs 2-2 Austin Peay and a nine-point win over 0-4 Winthrop, and two warmups vs Division II squads. They currently sit 163rd on KenPom.
 Alabama has won both previous meetings between the programs, including a 92-81 victory last December in Huntsville.
 Players to Watch: 
 F Amir Taylor, 6’9” sophomore 
 Taylor was a major recruiting pull for Pettway last season as a three-star big from nearby Grayson, GA. He has emerged this season as perhaps the most complete player on the roster, averaging nearly 12 points with eight rebounds. He has even managed to knock down 60% of his three point attempts thus far, albeit on very low volume. Against Winthrop he put up 19 points and grabbed nine rebounds, four offensive, in only 21 minutes of action. He could be a problem if Alabama continues to treat rebounding as an afterthought.
 F Kyler Theophile, 6’6” freshman 
 Theophile was an unheralded recruit but has been an early surprise, leading the undefeated Owls in scoring at 12 points per game. The 6’6” freshman from Coral Springs, Florida, has shot 41% from three on four attempts in 20 minutes per night, so the Tide will need to know where he is at all times.
 G Jacoby Hill, 6’5” sophomore 
 A transfer from Jacksonville State, Hill serves as the primary ballhandler for the Owls. He’s a steady presence on the floor who does his best work getting to the rim, and is a tough defender with solid size. He isn’t likely to hurt you much from behind the arc.
 F Avery Thomas II, 6’8” junior 
 Another active big that Alabama will have to contend with, Thomas arrives from Louisiana Tech, where he started 26 games for the Bulldogs and earned All-Tournament honors. The 213-pound forward has started all three games he’s played for Kennesaw State this season, averaging 10 points, six boards, and a team-leading 2.0 blocks per contest.
 F Trey Simpson, 6’8” sophomore 
 Simpson returns as one of Kennesaw State’s most important players after earning preseason All-Conference USA recognition. The Evergreen, Alabama native is another frontcourt option who can operate away from the basket and create matchup problems for smaller defenders. His ability to compete against Alabama’s bigger, more athletic forwards will be important.
 G Kris Parker, 6’9” senior 
 Parker is a familiar name for Alabama fans, having originally signed with the Crimson Tide as part of its 2023 recruiting class. The Tallahassee native redshirted his only season in Tuscaloosa before transferring to UCF and eventually landing at Kennesaw State. At 6’9”, Parker has elite length for a wing. This will be his first trip to Tuscaloosa as an opposing player.
 Three Keys: 
 1. Can Alabama take care of the basketball? 
 Alabama’s ball security was disgusting last time out against a game Seton Hall squad. The level of competition dips considerably in this one, but the Tide has double digit turnovers in every game this season, averaging 13 a night. This is not a recipe for success going forward, as this is the last tune-up before the Tide’s annual gauntlet kicks off next week.
 2. Will the Tide rebound? 
 The frontcourt is a strength for Kennesaw State, but they don’t match up with Alabama’s bigs from a talent perspective. There are no excuses for losing on the glass tonight. Like ball security, this is an area that will need to improve if Alabama is going to make any noise in the SEC and NCAA tournament.
 3. What will the rotation look like tonight? 
 Alabama’s freshmen showed out in the first couple of games, but had a tough time against Seton Hall. Jaxon Richardson led the group with 11 minutes and Qayden Samuels got 10, but they combined for six turnovers in those limited minutes while Anderson Diaz and Tarris Bouie barely saw the floor. Nate said that Bouie was dealing with an injury, so that will be something to monitor, but for whatever reason Oats essentially shortened the rotation to seven against the Pirates, with Cole Cloer and Keitenn Bristow acting as the top reserves. Hopefully the youngsters can get some time on the floor tonight and build some confidence. They showed flashes of promise in early action.
 How to Watch: 
 Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
 Tipoff: 6:30 p.m. CT
 Location: Coleman Coliseum
 TV: None
 Streaming: ESPN app/SEC Network+
